questions.prompt: A command you ran in every repo for a year has suddenly started producing a different, worse result on a task it used to nail. Which distinction tells you where to look?
options: It is a prompt-based entry, so the variation comes from the model reading the instructions in a different context — re-read and sharpen them
It is a fixed built-in, so the output should be identical every time — check the harness version and the --debug log
It is fixed logic either way, so the cause is your conversation history being too long
It depends on nothing — commands that behave differently across projects are always a bug in the skill listing budget
questions.explanation: Fixed built-in commands run the same harness code on the same input, so variation across repos means something environmental changed — a version, a setting, or a permission boundary — and --debug is where that shows up. Option A swaps the categories: it is exactly the prompt-based failure mode, and those entries vary because the model varies. Option C assumes history leaks into a deterministic code path, which it cannot. Option D invents a mechanism — the listing budget decides whether a skill is described to the model, not whether a command's output varies.

questions.prompt: You want a one-liner that opens a pull request, and you are fairly sure the name is /pr. What is the right first move?
options: Type /pr and read the error, which lists the closest valid names
Type /pr and if it fails try /pull-request, /open-pr, /pr-open until one works
Open the slash menu and check whether any entry does it, then run /help to confirm the exact name and alias
Skip the built-in one and write your own — the built-ins never cover a workflow as small as this
questions.explanation: The menu autocompletes on every character, so it answers 'does this exist' in one keystroke, and /help confirms the exact name and its alias. Option A bets on an error message listing near-misses; that is not something the CLI guarantees. Option B is the guessing loop from the lesson's opening problem — four wrong guesses and a paragraph retyped by hand. Option C's error is the last one: reaching for a custom command before checking what ships is how the retyped paragraph happened in the first place.

questions.prompt: Before adding your own skills to this project, what is the most useful thing to run and why?
options: /clear, so the baseline is measured on an empty window
/doctor, to confirm no skill is currently installed and charging you for its listing
/context, so you have a before-grid you can compare against once the listing has a cost
/compact, to keep the grid small enough to compare later
questions.explanation: A baseline needs to be comparable to a later reading, and /context is what gives you that reading — the Skills row is where a listing's cost shows up once you have skills. Option A is backwards: clearing mid-session destroys the very history you'd want to compare against, and costs you the work. Option B is close but off-target — /doctor estimates listing cost, which is useful once things exist, and it is not a stored before/after measurement. Option D is destructive for a reason unrelated to measurement.
